blocks.h2: Should Your Algonquin Basement Have an Overhead Sewer?

tiles.h3: Water Rises at the Floor Drain in Storms
tiles.body: Then drains away once the rain stops.
No roots or sag, and it still happens.
High water puts more load on the sewer.

blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: An overhead system takes the basement off gravity drainage. The floor drain and basement fixtures drain into a sealed pit. An [ejector pump](/algonquin/ejector-pump) lifts the water to a pipe near the ceiling, a check valve keeps it from falling back and it leaves the house above the level the sewer can reach. When the sewer surcharges, there's no low opening for water to come through.

blocks.h2: Do Algonquin Homes Need Overhead Sewers?
blocks.intro: Many Algonquin homes are newer, but a newer house can still have gravity basement drains.

items.body: Some homes from the 1990s and 2000s already have an ejector pit for a basement bathroom but still drain the floor drain by gravity. That floor drain is where storm water can come up.
When the Fox River is high, as in April 2013 and July 2017, more water gets into sewer systems.
More than half of Algonquin homes went up between 1990 and 2009, many with finished lower levels.
We camera your line before recommending a conversion. A [sewer repair](/algonquin/sewer-repair) may be all you need.

blocks.h2: Which Protection Does Your Basement Need?
blocks.intro: Sump pumps, backflow valves and overhead sewers each stop a different kind of water:
head: Sump Pump
Backflow Valve
Overhead Sewer System
rows: Groundwater rising under and around the basement
Sewer water flowing backward into the drain
Sewer water rising through any basement drain in a storm
A pit, a pump and a discharge line
A valve with a flap on the main line
A sealed pit, an ejector pump and new overhead piping
Homes near the river with high groundwater
Homes with a simple layout and occasional backups
blocks.note: We'll tell you which ones your basement needs.

blocks.h2: Overhead Sewer Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: Do newer Algonquin homes already have overhead sewers?
items.preview: Some do. Look for a sealed pit with a pump and a pipe going up.
items.answer: Some do. If your basement has a sealed pit with a pump and a pipe running up toward the ceiling, you may already have one. We can confirm in one visit.

items.q: Will an overhead sewer stop groundwater?
items.preview: No. That's a sump pump's job.
items.answer: No. It stops sewer backups. Groundwater needs a [sump pump](/algonquin/sump-pumps).
Yes. It drains to the new pit along with the rest of the basement.
Usually a few days, depending on the layout and how finished the basement is.

items.q: What does an overhead sewer system cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on your basement. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on sewer depth, layout, fixtures and access. We quote a flat rate before we start.
